\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Correlated Gaussian measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p004-b001}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
For a natural number $n$ and real number $\rho$, take two independent vectors
$Z_1,Z_2\in\mathbb{R}^n$ whose coordinates are independent standard Gaussian random
variables. The correlated Gaussian measure with parameter $\rho$ is the distribution of
$\bigl(Z_1,\,\rho Z_1+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Z_2\bigr)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p004-b001}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p010-b007}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
For a natural number $n$, a real parameter $\rho$, a function
$f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, the Gaussian noise operator
at $x$ is the Gaussian average of $f\bigl(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y\bigr)$, where $Y$
has independent standard Gaussian coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian noise stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p004-b001}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002,
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b003
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
For a natural number $n$, a real parameter $\rho$, and a function
$f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, its Gaussian noise stability is
$\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[f(X)\,T_\rho f(X)]$, where $X$ has independent standard
Gaussian coordinates and $T_\rho f$ is the Gaussian noise operator with parameter
$\rho$.
\end{definition}
